prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a rounded foreground rock ledge within 0.5–2.5 m of the camera wearer, a seated companion in a green hoodie about 1.2–1.8 m away in front, and steep canyon cliff walls dropping off into the background several metres to tens of metres behind and below the ledge. The camera wearer's own legs and shoes appear brightest at the bottom edge (roughly 0.4–0.8 m away, within the wearer's arm's reach along with the near end of the coiled climbing rope at 0.8–1.5 m), while the companion sits roughly 1 m beyond the wearer's feet, facing right and angled slightly away from the camera wearer with the rope and metal anchor chains within his arm's reach. Across the five frames, the camera wearer's head pans and tilts upward and to the right, causing the companion and foreground boulder to shift from the upper-left/centre in frames 1–3 toward the lower-right in frame 4 and almost entirely out of the left frame edge by frame 5, where only his hands and feet remain visible. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the sharp foreground ledge boundary from the dark shadowed cliff drop-off behind it and shows the continuous 3D slope of the dome rock. However, the depth map is unreliable on thin structures like the coiled rope and metal anchor chains, which blend into the rock surface after frame 1, and it flattens distant rock formations and sky into uniform black or flat grey planes without metric detail.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the seated companion (`person`, pink mask) about 1.2–1.8 m in front of the camera wearer across all five frames and detects the camera wearer's own lower left leg and shoe (`person`, brown-pink mask) at the bottom-left of frame 1 around 0.5–0.8 m away. In frame 1, the companion's head is cropped out of the top edge while his torso and arms reach down toward the rope within his arm's reach; across frames 2–5, as the camera turns right and upward, the companion shifts from the left-centre to the lower-right and is mostly cropped out at the bottom-left edge of frame 5. The companion's right arm and torso self-occlude his left side and legs as he faces right and looks downward toward his hands rather than toward the camera wearer. While the segmentation mask provides sharp silhouette boundaries for the companion against the dark cliff background that are harder to separate at a glance in RGB, it completely misses the coiled climbing rope, metal anchor chains, and the camera wearer's legs in frames 2–3. It is also unreliable in frame 4, where the rounded sandstone boulder ledge (0.5–2 m away) is falsely segmented and mislabelled as a `surfboard` next to the companion.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D body and hand keypoints for the seated companion in frames 2, 3, and 4 at roughly 1.2–1.8 m from the camera wearer, while detecting no skeletons in frames 1 and 5. The yellow upper-body and facial keypoints show the companion in right-profile facing toward the right of the frame and looking down toward his lap and hands—never looking toward the camera wearer—with his arms reaching forward and down to manipulate the rope within his arm's reach. Across frames 2 to 4, the skeleton translates from the left-centre to the lower-right of the image as the camera pans right, with the lower body and legs largely omitted or cropped near the bottom frame boundary and the left arm partly occluded behind the right arm in profile. The pose map makes the exact articulation of the shoulders, elbows, wrists, head tilt, and clustered magenta finger joints in frame 2 explicit even where the dark green hoodie and shadows obscure joint centres in the RGB image. However, it is unreliable when body parts are partly out of view, failing completely in frame 1 (where the companion's head is cropped at the top edge) and frame 5 (where only his hands and feet remain inside the left edge), as well as missing the camera wearer's visible legs and the companion's hands in frames 3–4.
